headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: Shark sightings prompt warning at Monterey County beaches
headlines.description: Another shark sighting along the Monterey County coast is putting beachgoers on alert. Pacific Grove police are advising people to stay out of the water at Lovers Point Beach after sharks were spotted in the area. While the beach remains open, officials say swimming, surfing and other water activities are not recommended. The warning comes just days after drone video captured five great white sharks about 200 yards off a beach near Sanctuary Beach Resort in Marina. Animal experts say it’s common for sharks to return to the Central Coast during the fall and urge beachgoers to use extra caution.

headlines.title: Game 6 of WNBA Finals set for early tipoff Thursday at State Farm Arena
headlines.description: Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between the Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries will be played at State Farm Arena on Thursday at 12:30 p.m. ET/9:30 a.m. PT, the league announced a few hours before Game 5 was set to take place on Monday. The WNBA worked hard with the NBA to move the game to State Farm Arena — home of the Atlanta Hawks — where Games 3 and 4 of the championship series were played. The Hawks have a game against the Cleveland Cavaliers that night that couldn’t be moved to another date or place. The only way they could make it work was to play the early afternoon game. The Hawks’ game against the Cavaliers was moved back an hour. “The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere at State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success, and we’re excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line,” WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert said. “We thank the NBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for the collaboration and flexibility that made this move possible. We look forward to delivering another unforgettable Finals experience in Atlanta.” Game 5 will start at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT Monday in San Francisco. By playing Game 6 in State Farm Arena, the Dream can have more than 17,000 fans as opposed to their normal home of Gateway Center Arena, which seats about 3,500. Games 3 and 4 were sold out. It was the third time in the series that the WNBA made accommodations for the Dream to be able to play at the bigger arena. Game 3 was moved up a day to last Wednesday and Saturday’s contest started at 1 p.m. ET so the Hawks could still host their home opener that night against Houston. That game was moved back 30 minutes to allow more time for the arena staff to change the building over for the Hawks contest. Now there potentially could be a champion crowned that day so there will be more time between games. The NBA and WNBA explored options to keep the game in primetime.

headlines.title: Anthropic files for potentially the biggest IPO ever even as CEO warns of risk to humanity from AI
headlines.description: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic filed papers Monday for what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever even as its top executive warns that advanced AI could pose an existential threat to humanity. The filing sets up the San Francisco company for a Wall Street debut next month, potentially eclipsing the SpaceX initial public offering in June that raised a record $86 billion. An Anthropic IPO would also put the company ahead of OpenAI in going public in what is expected to be a pair of blockbuster stock debuts for the rival AI labs. The filing comes weeks after CEO Dario Amodei argued in an essay for slowing the development of the most advanced AI models. An IPO could provide Anthropic with enormous resources to accelerate its expansion. The amount the company ultimately raises remains uncertain, as do its final valuation and offering price, but even at lower estimates, it would turn the five-year-old startup into one of the world’s most valuable companies and potentially boost the wealth of Amodei and his sister and co-founder, Daniela, by billions of dollars. The 335-page document showed Anthropic’s revenue is growing rapidly, but like many other tech companies going public, it has yet to turn a profit. The company behind the chatbot Claude reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026. That compares to a loss of $13 billion in the same period a year earlier. Despite the losses, Anthropic, valued earlier this year at $965 billion by private investors, is reportedly set to see that value rise to $1.5 trillion or possibly $2 trillion, although its final valuation has not been established. At $1.5 trillion, Anthropic would rank among the world’s most valuable public companies, alongside Tesla. As for money raised, the offering could bring in as much as $100 billion, according to reports, surpassing the current record set by another one of Elon Musk’s companies, SpaceX, earlier this year. In a regulatory filing, Anthropic said it will list its stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT.” U.S. & World Artificial intelligence Oct 25 Artificial intelligence Sep 22 Artificial intelligence Sep 18 Risks aplenty, but a big payoff to the founders In the filing, the company said it could use some of that money on acquiring other businesses and technology as well as investing in infrastructure to grow its business to take on rivals. Formed in 2021 by ex-OpenAI leaders, Anthropic is locked in a fight for dominance with that company, and the two leaders, Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, are widely seen as bitter rivals. But they have plenty of other competitors, including Google, newer startups in the U.S. and China and Musk’s SpaceX, which has an AI business. Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX’s AI division have all been losing more money than they make because of the huge costs in resources in building AI, fueling concerns of a bubble. The IPO would help cover any cash shortfall as well as shower extraordinary wealth on Anthropic’s seven founders, including Amodei and his sister. Collectively they own nearly 500 million shares, though it’s unclear from the offering document how much that will represent of the company after the IPO. Dario, 43, and 39-year-old Daniela, who is Anthropic’s president, are worth $15.5 billion each, according to Forbes, which ranks them as the 176th and 177th richest in the world. The filing also listed a host of risks for the San Francisco-based Anthropic, ranging from not being able to retain key staff, navigate regulatory roadblocks and secure enough compute power to run its AI systems. But the standout was that its AI models could “pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.” Calls for an AI slowdown The IPO comes as worries about AI grow inside and outside the industry and reports continue to emerge about increasingly powerful systems that solve problems beyond human capacity but could also go rogue and carry out other, more harmful tasks. In September, Amodei said the AI industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without such a slowdown, Amodei warned AI could be capable of letting loose a swarm of agents that could take over the entire internet within six to 12 months. He offered a plan in a post on his website to increase checks on the industry, noting that Anthropic is already undertaking part of this on its own. As for other steps, though, he said that would require coordination across the industry and with governments around the world, including authoritarian ones. “I believe that if slowing down bought us even an extra year or two before models reach critical levels of capability, and we used that time to advance alignment, we could greatly reduce the risk that something goes seriously wrong,” Amodei wrote. Clashes with the U.S. government Anthropic has tried to set itself apart from other AI companies as the “good guys,” focusing on safety and responsible development as opposed to growing at all costs and with few guardrails. Some of this sentiment stems from the company’s dispute with the U.S. government, which broke out in February when President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth accused Anthropic of endangering national security and designated the company a supply chain risk. Anthropic sued the Pentagon over the supply chain risk designation in March for what it called an “unlawful campaign of retaliation” over its refusal to allow unrestricted military use of its technology. The legal challenge intensified an unusually public dispute over how AI can be used in warfare and mass surveillance. ChatGPT maker OpenAI made its own deal to work with the Pentagon hours after the government punished Anthropic for its stance. Anthropic also filed a separate and narrower case involving a different rule the Pentagon is using to try to declare Anthropic a supply chain risk. A California judge ruled in Anthropic’s favor in the first case and a Washington D.C. judge sided with the government in the second. Both sides are appealing the decisions.
headlines.source: Barbara Ortutay and Bernard Condon | The Associated Press

headlines.title: San Pablo police investigate homicide after man found dead in car
headlines.description: Police in San Pablo are investigating a homicide after a man was found unresponsive in his car on Sunday, the department said. Just before 2:30 p.m., officers responded to the 1600 block of 16th Street following a report of a male who was possibly deceased inside a parked vehicle. Police located the 33-year-old San Pablo man inside a red Toyota. He was unresponsive and had apparent injuries, the department said. First responders arrived to assess the man medically, but he was pronounced dead at the scene. San Pablo Police Department detectives are investigating the man’s death as a homicide, and the investigation remains active, with no suspects named. Anyone with information regarding this case is encouraged to contact the San Pablo Police Department at 510-215-3150

headlines.title: Rare corpse flower set to bloom at UC Santa Cruz
headlines.description: A corpse flower is expected to bloom at the University of California, Santa Cruz this week. The rare plant is native to Sumatra, Indonesia. This particular corpse flower bloomed for the first time in 2022. Staff at the arboretum say it’s budding and expect it to bloom this week. When it blooms, the plant emits a rotten flesh smell to lure bugs deep into the plant so pollen will stick to them. Although the plant hasn’t bloomed yet, people are flocking to the UC Santa Cruz campus to check it out. The arboretum is selling T-shirts that say, “I sniffed the UCSC Arboretum corpse flower.” The arboretum will let the public know on social media when the flower blooms and will extend viewing hours that day.

headlines.title: High tides pose minor coastal flooding risk across the Bay Area
headlines.description: High tides could cause minor flooding in low-lying coastal areas across the San Francisco Bay Area through Saturday, potentially affecting roads, infrastructure and beaches, the National Weather Service said. The risk includes bayshore locations along San Pablo Bay, San Francisco Bay and Monterey Bay, as well as low-lying areas along the Pacific coast, according to an NWS advisory on Monday. At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is forecast to peak at 1.9 feet above normal Wednesday, reaching 7.7 feet above mean lower low water. The forecast calls for tides 1.8 feet above normal Tuesday and 1.7 feet above normal Monday and Thursday. The agency warned that high tides could flood low-lying infrastructure, cause isolated road closures and contribute to coastal erosion. Rising water and waves could also reach farther up beaches than usual, making it harder for people to leave coastal areas safely. People are advised to allow extra travel time if roads are affected, avoid driving around barricades or through water of unknown depth, and protect property in flood-prone areas. Cool conditions are expected through the week, with a 20% to 40% chance of rain from Friday into the weekend. Confidence in the rain forecast is low to moderate, and the unsettled pattern could continue into early next week, the NWS said.

headlines.title: 9th Circuit questions DOJ demand to set aside 20,000 California mail ballots
headlines.description: A panel of federal appellate judges on Sunday questioned the timing, constitutionality and authority of the Justice Department’s demand that California election officials set aside thousands of mail ballots from people the federal government suspects may not be citizens. During rare weekend arguments, two of the three judges on the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals appeared skeptical of a lawsuit brought by President Donald Trump’s administration in mid-October. The lawsuit accuses California officials of failing to meet a 48-hour deadline to review 20,000 names the administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the state’s voter rolls. The administration asked a federal judge to require the state to withhold counting those ballots until the voters’ immigration status could be verified. The district judge scheduled a hearing for Oct. 27, days after the case was assigned, but the federal government appealed to the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals, seeking an expedited decision. Justice Department attorney Matthew Donnelly told the panel that California is causing irreparable harm “by allowing noncitizens to vote in violation of their own state laws. The damage is irreversible and irrevocable.” The Trump administration has made efforts to identify noncitizen voters a priority this year, even though noncitizen voting is exceptionally rare. Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, a Trump appointee, questioned whether the appellate court even has jurisdiction to hear the case even before a ruling by the lower court. Donnelly argued that the schedule set by the lower court judge was too slow and effectively a denial of the government’s request, as state elections officials process thousands of mail ballots every day. Judge Gabriel Sanchez, appointed by former President Joe Biden, questioned whether the federal government was violating the Tenth Amendment, essentially commandeering the state to enforce a federal law that makes it a misdemeanor for a noncitizen to vote. The federal government is simply asking California to enforce its own law, which also bans noncitizens from voting, Donnelly said. He argued the state’s refusal to comply with the federal request to set aside the ballots for review was “frustrating the purpose” of the federal law against noncitizen voting. The Elections Clause of the U.S. Constitution gives state legislatures the power to set the time, place and manner of congressional elections, Bennett said. The executive branch may be “unhappy with what they’re doing, and doesn’t like the manner,” Bennett said, but under the Election Clause the state has the right to determine those issues — including how it sorts out any noncitizen voters. Attorney Seth Waxman, representing Los Angeles County Clerk Dean Logan, said the federal government’s list was unreliable and that segregating the ballots for a review process would effectively disenfranchise thousands of eligible voters. Even if election staffers spent just three minutes checking each of the expected 2.75 million mail ballots against the government’s list, the process would take 140,000 man-hours, Waxman said — or about 16 years of working time. Waxman cited a review of 200 records from the Trump administration’s list conducted by Los Angeles County staffers. Assistant Registrar-Recorder Monica Flores said in a court filing that the sample included canceled or inactive registrations, individuals with no voting history and voters who appeared to have been born in the United States, which the filing notes “is strong evidence of citizenship.” If the administration disagrees with how California runs its elections, it can ask Congress to change that process, said attorney Sam Siegel, representing California Secretary of State Shirley Weber. The federal government has provided no credible evidence to support its suspicions, said Siegel. “It has no basis in law or in fact,” he told the panel. “We just dispute the premise that noncitizens are voting.” But Judge Patrick Bumatay, who was appointed by Trump, said everyone has an interest in ensuring that only eligible citizens vote. He suggested that granting the administration’s request for an emergency order could provide clarity. “Without an injunction, you will never know” if that is happening, Bumatay told Siegel. Bennett said the panel would try to issue a ruling as quickly as possible. ___ Boone reported from Boise, Idaho. ___ This story was first published Oct. 25, 2026. It was updated Oct. 26, 2026, to correct the name of the attorney who represents California’s secretary of state. He is Sam Siegel, not Siegal or Seigel.

headlines.title: Man accused of attacking his neighbor with a machete in San Jose
headlines.description: A man was accused of attacking his neighbor with a machete and then barricading himself in his home during a hourslong standoff in San Jose on Sunday, police said. Police said officers responded to the 1800 block of Naples Drive around 9:07 a.m. after receiving a report of a disturbance involving a weapon. The preliminary investigation revealed a man assaulted his neighbor with a machete, according to authorities. The police department said the victim was taken to the hospital and was later released. The victim, Alberto Cuevas, said he’s had other run ins with the same neighbor in the past. He says the assault happened as he went to take his garbage out in the morning. “My wife looked at me. I was crouched down when he struck me. He grabbed me from behind, but I managed to react a little shifting to the side, so he only caught me on the side. Otherwise, he might’ve split my head open,” Cuevas said. “Honestly, you feel afraid and frustrated because there’s nothing you can do and then you are left bleeding.” Cuevas said he received stitches to his head. After the attack, the suspect entered his own home and refused to come out, triggering a standoff. More than seven hours later, police moved toward the home and a man in handcuffs came out, surrounded by officers. Officials said this is an ongoing investigation. Police have not yet released the name of the specific crimes the suspect was arrested for.

headlines.title: ICE agents spotted at San Jose jail, advocates say
headlines.description: Advocates with the Santa Clara County Rapid Response Network said ICE agents were present in the lobby of the Main Jail on Hedding Street in San Jose on Sunday. Advocates responded to the jail in the morning. They said agents were just outside the building as well, apparently waiting for people to be released. On Saturday, members of the same network were at the Elmwood Jail in Milpitas, watching ICE agents there for a third day in a row. Activists want to make it very clear to the agents that their actions are being witnessed and documented. Santa Clara County is a sanctuary county, but no sanctuary policy can prohibit agents from waiting in public areas of the jail. The sheriff’s office says that it does not coordinate with ICE or notify the agency of release dates. They have been tracking ICE visits as well and say agents have been visiting the lobby for more than a year, and taken 60 people into custody who were set for release. NBC Bay Area reached out to ICE for comment on Sunday’s activity but has not heard back.

headlines.title: Temporary closure of Alcatraz worries San Francisco vendors
headlines.description: One of San Francisco’s most iconic tourist attractions is shutting down completely for three weeks for repairs, leaving Embarcadero vendors worried about lost business and tourists holding tickets they can’t use. “The Rock” will close starting Monday through Nov. 19. The National Park Service said repairs are needed on pilings that support the ferry dock on Alcatraz Island, and that means there will be no ferries leaving Pier 33 for three weeks. That closure also means the area will lose thousands of daily visitors for three straight weeks, which is a concern for small businesses, especially vendors who set up shop daily at Pier 33. Carmen, the owner of Nothing But Fruits, said she won’t lose 100% of her business, but she will lose a lot and it worries her because business is always bad when Alcatraz closes. Jose D., a pedicab operator with Golden Gate Pedicabs, said he’ll make route adjustments until the tours start again. “I won’t be stopping here. This is our zone and I won’t be waiting here anymore, probably the next few weeks or so,” Jose D. said. The island will be completely shut down, meaning no public tours, cell house visits or private drop-offs until the repairs are completed. Anyone with existing tickets scheduled during the closure will get refunds or be offered alternative tour dates.

headlines.title: Defense questions FBI agent in Sheng Thao corruption trial
headlines.description: The defense on Monday questioned one of the FBI agents who investigated former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao for her role in an alleged bribery and corruption scheme. The defense is trying to challenge testimony involving businessman Mario Juarez, one of the government’s key witnesses. Juarez has already pleaded guilty in the case and is expected to testify against the four defendants, including Thao, in hopes of receiving a lighter sentence. On Monday, the attorney for co-defendant Andy Duong questioned FBI Special Agent Katherine Barclay for a second day. Barclay has testified about photos, texts, calls, videos and financial records as prosecutors try to prove that Thao, Andy Duong, his father David and Thao’s longtime boyfriend Andre Jones were part of a bribery and corruption scheme to help Thao get elected and siphon money to Jones in exchange for favors to the Duong family. The Duongs own California Waste Solutions, Oakland’s recycling contractor. All four defendants in the criminal case have pleaded not guilty. Andy Duong’s attorney argues there is no audio proof his client bribed Thao and no evidence the Duongs ever received any of the city contracts or contract extensions prosecutors claim were part of the deal. Prosecutors say simply pursuing a “pay for access” deal is a crime, even if it ultimately fell apart. Barclay spent all of Monday on the witness stand. With four defendants in the case, each witness can be cross-examined four separate times. Once the jury was dismissed for the day, the judge took the opportunity to somewhat admonish each of the defense attorneys for taking too long in questioning the witness, telling them, “You can try the case anyway you want, but those jurors’ eyes are glazing over.” The trial is expected to resume Tuesday morning.
